name: Sabine Baring-Gould
knownFor: Parson, antiquarian, novelist and folk-song collector; author of "Onward, Christian Soldiers".

works.title: Curious Myths of the Middle Ages
Mehalah: a Story of the Salt Marshes
Songs and Ballads of the West
works.note: folk songs collected in Devon and Cornwall, with H. Fleetwood Sheppard

events.text: Took his B.A. at Clare College, Cambridge (M.A. 1860).
Ordained, and became curate at Horbury Bridge in Yorkshire.
Married Grace Taylor, a mill-hand's daughter he had met as a curate; they had fifteen children.
Became rector of East Mersea in Essex.
Inherited the Lew Trenchard estate in Devon on his father's death; he later became its squire and rector.
Began publishing Songs and Ballads of the West, the fruit of years of collecting folk songs from farm labourers in Devon and Cornwall.
Died at Lew Trenchard and was buried beside his wife.

relevance: A working parson who wrote on folklore, saints, travel, hymns and fiction, he collected the songs and stories of the Devon countryside at a time when few others were doing it systematically. The Book of Were-Wolves was one of his first books.
influence: Cecil Sharp dedicated English Folk Song: Some Conclusions (1907) to him. His hymn "Onward, Christian Soldiers" is still sung, and Lew Trenchard Manor, which he rebuilt, is now a hotel.
